introducedIn.note: Cloud OAuth2 support added; routeOAuth2Complete never received the checkAuth wrapper its pre-existing OAuth1 sibling (routeOAuth1Complete) already had. No commit message, comment, or design doc found explaining a deliberate asymmetry -- reads as an oversight relative to the established OAuth1 pattern in the same file set.

relatedButDistinctIssues.summary: Logout CSRF disconnecting a user's Jira connection via a crafted message action.
relatedButDistinctIssues.distinguishedFrom: Does not touch server/user_cloud_oauth.go or the OAuth2 state-parsing/account-linking path; a different handler and a different (disconnection, not linking) impact.

relatedButDistinctIssues.summary: httpShareIssuePublicly and httpTransitionIssuePostAction trusting an attacker-suppliable UserId field in the JSON action payload.
relatedButDistinctIssues.distinguishedFrom: Same general bug CLASS (trusting a client-supplied identity instead of the verified session) but a different pair of handlers, unrelated to the OAuth2 completion flow.

relatedButDistinctIssues.summary: A crafted action leaking Jira issue details.
relatedButDistinctIssues.distinguishedFrom: Different handler/impact (information disclosure), unrelated to OAuth2 state handling.

conclusion: The three disclosed CVEs are related but mechanically distinct from server/user_cloud_oauth.go. No public advisory, issue, or pull request covering this exact callback path was found. This supports only 'no public match found'; private program reports remain unknowable, so novelty and duplicate status are not proven.
verificationMethod: Public GitHub issues, commits, advisories, and web search plus component-level execution against the real handler with Atlassian HTTP responses mocked.
